chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"When you rise from prostration, say: 'O Allah, by Your power and strength I rise and sit. And if You will, say: and I bow and prostrate.'
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication to recite when rising from prostration in prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith prescribes a specific dhikr for rising from prostration, distinguishing between the physical capability granted by Allah’s power (quwwa) and the spiritual acts of worship performed by His will (shi'). This distinction highlights the Shia emphasis on recognizing divine agency in both bodily movement and ritual obedience, reinforcing the concept of *tawakkul* during the physical transitions of Salah.
